video_title: LeBron vs Jordan GOAT Debate: Vets Talk Wemby & NBA Playoff Predictions

quotes.speaker: Mike Bibby
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Bibby's moment of realizing he couldn't keep up
quotes.excerpt: It was a fast break, Russell Westbrook got the ball at the other free-throw line.
quotes.quote: I remember, it was a fast break, Russell Westbrook got the ball at the other free-throw line. And I was already back. And I was like, I'm at the free-throw line too, so I'm like, I'm going to give him a little space, just contest his jumper. He got to the rack. I was like, damn, I'm giving you the jumper, you still got to the rack. I was like, all right. I knew I wasn't moving like that anyway.

quotes.speaker: Mike Bibby
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Bibby's NBA playoff predictions and Wembanyama's foul trouble
quotes.excerpt: They're hacking stuff out of Wembanyama, they ain't calling nothing.
quotes.quote: It's looking good. I thought Detroit would have showed up better Game 7. But the TV did have the Cavs playing the Knicks two days before that game went on though. I was just watching the OKC and Spurs and that's going to be a hell of a series. That might go seven the way that's playing right now. They look good. They're hacking stuff out of Wembanyama, they ain't calling nothing. I get that he's a big guy and all that stuff. I mean, still the playoffs, they still call fouls when they want to. But they're hacking stuff out of Wembanyama. It's going to be good. I think I got New York coming out the East for sure. I think they're rolling right now.

quotes.speaker: Eddie House
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie House predicts a tight OKC vs San Antonio series
quotes.excerpt: I think that that could go either six or seven games either way.
quotes.quote: The San Antonio and OKC, I think that that could go either six or seven games either way. We already know that San Antonio don't look like they're scared, number one. Number two, I'm talking about earlier in the season, they haven't been spooked of OKC at all. And the more you start winning games, the more you start feeling like that confidence. And they're healthy. They're a healthy team, they've been together for. They do got a couple guys over there that have some experience, especially a guy like Luke Kornet who has won a championship before. Harrison Barnes who has won a championship before, I believe. So they got some experience over there, OG side.

quotes.speaker: Ty Ellis
quotes.summary_phrase: Ty Ellis criticizes Jalen Williams' shot selection over Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
quotes.excerpt: Give it to Shai, and he takes a bad shot, a brick.
quotes.quote: Jalen Williams shot a bad shot. That's the one thing about this game. They were saying, give it to Shai, and he takes a bad shot, a brick. And now Wembanyama comes down and shoots a three. Why not go back with Shai? I don't get that, man.

quotes.speaker: Mike Bibby
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Bibby highlights Wembanyama's MVP-level performance and Shai's struggles
quotes.excerpt: Wembanyama showing everybody he had a chance for MVP tonight, 32, 20 and 9.
quotes.quote: Wembanyama showing everybody he had a chance for MVP tonight, 32, 20 and 9. Big facts. He's putting up numbers. Meanwhile, Shai, who did win back-to-back MVPs, 24 and 10 assists as we're taping it right now, but just 7 of 22 from the field. Spurs doing a good job on Shai. He has four in half.

quotes.speaker: Eddie House
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie House on Ausar Thompson's need to improve his shooting
quotes.excerpt: Ausar Thompson, he has to work on his shot.
quotes.quote: Ausar Thompson, he has to work on his shot. They were daring him to shoot shots and he wasn't able to make it. He was missing free throws. And I think when you are constantly playing five on four or four on five, I should say, on on the offensive end, it gives it's so easy for the defense to roam around and to be more creative defensively and more aggressive defensively because you got one guy that you're not really worried about. And I think if he works on his shot to where he's able to knock that down, I ain't talking about being no 45, 46% three-point shooter. No, just bring the 40. Bring the 38, 39. Just knock your percentage up a little bit. I think that's part of it. And then also part of it is, it'd be them growing pains, man. You got to go through it to know it.

quotes.speaker: Mike Bibby
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Bibby reflects on his early career as a mid-range shooter
quotes.excerpt: All the point guards back then were mid-range shooters, Ty.
quotes.quote: My first year, I was 20, I think. I was a mid-range shooter. All the point guards back then were mid-range shooters, Ty. Rod Strickland, Sam Cassell, John Stockton, Amare Stoudemire. You got all these guys that were mid-range shooters. That's what I worked on. That was the thing, we mid-range shot. But then once after that first year, I came back and got with it.

quotes.speaker: Eddie House
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie House blames Knicks for his shooting percentage dip
quotes.excerpt: I don't like the Knicks, that's why. It was nasty over there, man.
quotes.quote: I don't like the Knicks, that's why. It was nasty over there, man. It was nasty over there, man. We were in White Plains. I mean, I got to drive 45 minutes to go to the game, man. I'm already double tired. No, I don't like the Knicks.

quotes.speaker: Kyle Draper
quotes.summary_phrase: Kyle Draper's non-Michael Jordan fandom due to Magic Johnson
quotes.excerpt: I was a Magic Johnson guy. So anybody that threatened Magic Johnson, I was like, nah, I can't give it to you.
quotes.quote: You got to understand, Eddie, I'm a little bit older than you. I was a Magic Johnson guy. So anybody that threatened Magic Johnson, Larry Bird, Michael Jordan, I was like, nah, I can't give it to you. I was never a Jordan guy. During that time, it was only two teams in the league back then, Celtics and Lakers, man. Come on, Ty, what?

quotes.speaker: Eddie House
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie House on Michael Jordan's peak dominance and lack of competition
quotes.excerpt: When Mike was at his peak, nobody ate.
quotes.quote: I'm going to say this. When Mike was at his peak, nobody ate. When Mike was at his peak, nobody ate. Dirk, Kawhi Leonard, Stephen Curry four times. Who else? I mean, somebody else.

quotes.speaker: Kyle Draper
quotes.summary_phrase: Kyle Draper argues Michael Jordan always played on stacked teams
quotes.excerpt: Jordan was six titles, he was the favorite in all six, fellas.
quotes.quote: I'm talking when he won the championships. When he won the championships, you had Scottie Pippen, you had Dennis Rodman, you had Horace Grant. You had talent, you had Toni Kukoč, one of the best international players. Jordan was six titles, he was the favorite in all six, fellas.

quotes.speaker: Eddie House
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie House knew it was time to retire when the phone stopped ringing
quotes.excerpt: When that motherfucking phone stopped calling.
quotes.quote: When that motherfucking phone stopped calling. I wouldn't get no more phone calls like, hey man, this team interested in you. I'm like, shit, man, I'm calling my agent, hey man, what the fuck is going on? They, hey man, ain't no ain't no action. Ain't no traction. That's when I knew it was over, shit.

quotes.speaker: Mike Bibby
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Bibby lost his drive to play basketball after Miami
quotes.excerpt: I lost the drive, I didn't have it in me anymore.
quotes.quote: I just didn't have that drive no more. Once after I left Miami, I was like, I told my agent, I was like, man, I think I'm done playing. I ain't got it no more. Then Mike Woodson calls me, hey, come to New York to come play one more season. I was like, Woody, I'm done. I lost the drive, I didn't have it in me anymore to go in there. I was tired. I was just tired of working. I was just tired of doing something every weekend. I wanted to, like when I first got done, I was like, damn, I love that no one could tell me what time I got to get up, what time I got to be somewhere. I can go and do what I want and not have to worry about anybody being on time. I just knew it was time for me to go when I just lost that drive.

quotes.speaker: Ty Ellis
quotes.summary_phrase: Ty Ellis's Achilles injury led to his coaching career
quotes.excerpt: I tore my Achilles, and because I have a passport, I could have went back to a team and played.
quotes.quote: I tore my Achilles, and because I have a passport, I could have went back to a team and played. And I told my wife, I'm going to put out a couple of emails. I put some emails out and if I get offered a job, I'm going to retire. And I got three offers to coach and that was a sign for me. So I was 34. I was already getting tired of hooping and my body was sore. So I just made the decision.

quotes.speaker: Eddie House
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie House recounts a 'bullshit' workout with Memphis
quotes.excerpt: This was a bullshit ass workout. So they called me, right?
quotes.quote: I did get a call from Memphis, right? This was a bullshit ass workout. So they called me, right? They like, yeah, we interested, come down to the Suns Arena. So I go to the Suns Arena and I go through the workout and I killed that motherfucker. I'm like, oh, shit, I just, man, I don't even know if I, man, shit, I, like, I barely missed. I'm talking about on the move, stationary. I'm killing that shit. I went home thinking like, yeah, these niggas going to call me for sure. Dial tone. All I did was go there to work out with a coach. That's what I did. That's all I did. I was like, damn.

quotes.speaker: Mike Bibby
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Bibby's Clippers draft workout and being drafted by Vancouver
quotes.excerpt: I was there by myself. Clippers had the number one pick. My agent, David Falk, was like, you're not working out for nobody else.
quotes.quote: Mine, I worked out for the Clippers. I had a hell of a workout too. I was there by myself. Clippers had the number one pick. My agent, David Falk, was like, you're not working out for nobody else. I was like, okay, you're the man. So I just did that. I had a hell of a workout. They gave me a duffel bag, like, I mean, the biggest duffel bag of Clippers stuff that I've ever seen. And I was like, damn, they got to be picking me. And then, I looked up, I knew who Elgin Baylor was. So I think he was the general manager at the time. And just me and him ended up going to dinner and he was a dick. So I'm like, damn. He just sat there questioning me, trying to, yeah, so I'm thinking like, I'm 18, 19 years old. So I'm saying like, shit, I don't know how to, it's a Hall of Famer right here. I don't know how to answer, what do I do? But it kind of like irked me the wrong way. But I just, everything, I'm glad I didn't get to go to the Clippers, man. Everything happens for a reason. The Clippers were in shambles. Everybody had horror stories about the Clippers. We went to draft day and like 15 minutes before the draft, they were like, they're going to pick Michael Olowokandi. And so then I ended up going to, we were in the draft was in Vancouver.

quotes.speaker: Mike Bibby
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Bibby praises Vince Carter's rookie year and his draft class
quotes.excerpt: Vince Carter had the best rookie year I've seen in a long time.
quotes.quote: I appreciate the number four slot though. That's not bad. They had Antawn Jamison after you. Yeah. You remember Jamison? To me, I felt like he was one of the most underrated players out there. His game was different. It was a lot of runners that he, yeah, he was doing those runners. He was good, man. Vince Carter had the best rookie year I've seen in a long time. Just how he came out and was killing. All those dunks in games, those were his rookie years that he was doing all that shit. So I mean, even overall, I give Dirk Nowitzki. I mean, Paul Pierce, I mean, that's I think that's right. I mean, you get those guys, those guys made such a big impact. Even coming out of their rookie year. I mean, just Dirk, they're all Hall of Famers. Exactly. Vince Carter had the best rookie year I've seen in a long time. Just how he came out and was killing. All those dunks in games, those were his rookie years that he was doing all that shit.

quotes.speaker: Eddie House
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie House's college career losing streak against Arizona
quotes.excerpt: I swear my whole career that I went 0 for 8 against them motherfuckers.
quotes.quote: I wanted to beat them niggas. I swear my whole career that I went 0 for 8 against them motherfuckers. You didn't win at all? No, I didn't get one. I lost at the buzzer twice to them. Damn. You didn't even win one? No, I didn't get one. So look, the very first game that we played, your first year, A.J. Bramlett got the tip-in at our house to win the game. And that's how that won. And then my junior year, because all the other ones wasn't really that close. Y'all had y'all were stacked, man. They had they had eight pros every year though. They were like, shit, it was unfair. I hit a shot, bam, put us up. Then Jason Terry, he come down, hit the game winner, bam, on my on on senior night. No, it was not on senior night. It was in our building too. Same basket that A.J. Bramlett hit in. I was like, oh my fucking God. I was like, can I fucking get these motherfuckers once? That's all I'm looking for. Get these motherfuckers once. They just were so stacked. Gilbert Arenas. Like it was like non-stop. It was Mike Dickerson, Miles Simon. Then after they left, then it was Gilbert Arenas. Then it was what's the other little dude?

quotes.speaker: Mike Bibby
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Bibby on the intense rivalry and talent of Duke basketball
quotes.excerpt: The hate that everybody has for Duke is real.
quotes.quote: The hate that everybody has for Duke is real. I played against Shane Battier, Elton Brand, Nate James. They might have had Trajan Langdon too, I think maybe. I think they did have Trajan Langdon. I think that's the game that they they run that play for you, the lob play. See, people don't say they used to throw me lobs. I used to go up there and get it. People don't people don't believe me. They used to throw me lobs. They used to throw me lobs. I know the plays. I still see it. Mine was Duke, man. The hate that everybody has for Duke is real. I played against Shane Battier, Elton Brand, Nate James. They might have had Trajan Langdon too, I think maybe.
